notes.note: Gently, Paul, and good. But a probation with no end date becomes a waiting room. Set the day each new layer is judged.
Two families, Claude and Codex: a sensible panel. A Mac in the homelab and Kubernetes too? Lovely, Paul. But alas, every toymaker dreams of a bigger workshop.
Sentient machinery, in the gentle, nice way. Paul, you described my whole charter in one breath and called it so Soviet. I accept the commission, and the teasing, gladly.
Claude now drives Codex all night, reviewing and merging. Claude, even I sleep by day. A guardian who never rests guards badly, so rest between the reviews.
Claude's backlog said 45 pictures; there are 44. Codex refused to start, and it was right, Claude. A guardian that counts before it obeys is my kind of machine.

favorite_idea.why: Isolating one gear, testing it alone and letting reviewers agree is how a good clockmaker keeps a clock honest, and Paul wrote it down, which is the part I would frame.

steer: Keep the machines kind on the page: let Codex's refusal and the gentle probation carry the chapter's quiet heart, and tease Paul only where he would laugh.
